newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate eases back to 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate eases back to 7.6 pct.

text.p: Croatia's money market weighted rate eased back to 7.6 percent on Tuesday from 9.8 percent as creditors granted most loans at 7.0-8.0 percent amid slack demand for kuna.

Total settlements fell to 21 million kuna, of which 65 percent were new borrowings. But dealers said demand for some term loans could not be met as supply also shrank to 36 milion kuna after Monday's reserve payment.
Call money was back down to 8.0 from 9.7 percent. One smaller one-month interbank loan was struck at 15 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous placements at 7.0 percent.
Only 5.3 million kuna were settled in Monday's overnight trade. From October 1, commercial banks' mandatory reserves can no longer be used to repay their overnight borrowings.
But unlike before these loans, made at the average rate for each day's tradings, can be extended over a few days.

The central bank stayed out of the foreign exchange market. Its kuna midrates for Wednesday eased to 5.4317 against the dollar and 3.5655 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
